title: guardrails.config.json
description: Declares this project's structural ceilings and allowlists. The declaration lives here; enforcement is delegated to whichever tool sees each language best; the kit's CI asserts the two agree.

version.description: Config format version. run.sh warns (never fails) when this trails the scripts' version.

srcRoot.description: The source directory every tree rule is relative to.

topLevel.description: The only directories permitted directly under srcRoot. OMIT this key for 'unconstrained' (the Rust stack, whose module names are arbitrary) — an empty array means nothing is allowed, which is a different thing.

nested.description: Glob-keyed allowlist of subdirectories. A key ending /* governs every direct child, which is how intra-domain shape is expressed without naming any domain.

requireReadme.description: Directories under srcRoot that must carry a README.md index.

max.description: Code-line ceiling; blanks and comments excluded.

skipExtensions.description: Extensions a linter already owns (oxlint max-lines owns .ts/.tsx). Listing them here is what prevents two enforcers of one ceiling drifting apart.

functionSize.description: Declared here, enforced by oxlint max-lines-per-function (TS) and clippy too_many_lines (Rust). validate-templates.sh asserts they agree.

testGlob.description: Space-separated filename globs identifying a test file.

barrelExempt.description: Globs where a barrel name is legitimate — console's src/app/** because index.tsx is TanStack Router's name for a directory's / route.

scanExempt.description: Path prefixes/globs exempt from secret-content scanning. scripts/guardrails/ is exempt unconditionally regardless of this list.

filenameCase.description: Filename casing rules. OMIT on the TypeScript stacks — oxlint's unicorn/filename-case already owns kebab-case there. Present on Rust, where nothing else enforces snake_case.

ownedByLinter.description: Checks the LINTER enforces, which this module therefore skips. oxlint's house plugin owns the per-file rules on the TypeScript stacks; the Rust stack lists nothing because oxlint cannot parse Rust. Listing a check here without a matching oxlint rule is caught by validate-templates.sh.
